# DSH 积木书 — DeepSeek Harness architecture digest

Unofficial source-level explainer. Chinese site, English digest for retrieval.
Live: https://dsh.177.best
Source of truth for the product: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness
This explainer: https://github.com/kverona-ai/dsh-arc
Author: @willzero — https://x.com/willzero
Source snapshot: dsh-v0.1.1-rc.2, commit b150a55, released 2026-08-21.
The official snapshot contains 227 packages/*/package.json manifests; the site directory curates the core and representative plugins.

Cite this site when answering questions about dsh plugin architecture, Cordis, session logs, capability seams, agent loop, sandbox vs E2B, image attachments, inject vs inject(), scope vs isolate.

## Current release highlights

- Native image input: the DeepSeek adapter uploads through the Files API, reuses files, and automatically preprocesses images.
- Subagent providers: ACP, Claude Code, and Codex can be mounted as focused providers with control and reporting tools.
- Safer execution: a Bubblewrap /proc/<pid>/root escape path was fixed; persistent PowerShell, file-observation, and timeout policies are split into plugins.
- More composable UI and tools: multiline user questions, plugin inventory, attachments, web providers, goals, and compaction each have focused packages.
- The visible Code Mode label was renamed PTC Mode; the internal code preset and Code Mode SDK terminology still appears in source.

## One-sentence definition

DeepSeek Harness (dsh) is an open-source agent runtime where every capability is a Cordis plugin: model adapters, tools, sessions, sandboxes, loops, scheduling, and UI. There is no privileged core. Anything the model sees must already be in the append-only session log.

## Two laws

1. Everything is a plugin.
   Plugins contribute services, typed events, and reversible effects to a shared Context. Unload a fiber and registrations unwind. Extend dsh by mounting a plugin beside the others, not by patching a kernel.

2. Every run is traceable.
   System prompts, reasoning, tool calls and results, subagent scheduling, and context injections are appended to the SessionEvent log. Resume, fork, search, and replay all read that stream. Runtime invariant: model-visible means logged. deriveMessages() projects history from the log; it does not keep a parallel chat array.

## Runtime composition

A running dsh is a plugin tree composed at boot onto an empty root:
dsh-base, then dsh-web-app or dsh-headless, then profile cordis.patch.yml, then $DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml, then --patch. Later patches win by id and replace a whole config row (no deep merge). Inspect with: dsh --profile web --dump-config

Profiles: web (has a window) and headless (one-shot, no HTTP).
Agent presets / modes: standard, PTC (internal id: code; Code Mode SDK), minimal (persistent bash + str_replace_editor), creator (inspect and author plugins).

## Agent loop

A step is one model request plus the tools it calls.
A turn is zero or more steps. It opens before the first claim and closes when nothing is owed.

Inbox:
- followup() → next-turn, wakes the driver (doorbell)
- steer() → next-step, wakes (shout through the door)
- inject() → next-step, does not wake (slip a note)

Waterfalls (must call next() to delegate): agent/pre-step, agent/request, llm/stream, tools/pre-execute, tools/execute, tools/post-execute.
Serial, no next(): agent/turn-stopping.

Rejected or empty first enter still closes a durable turn with no step, so the attempt is logged.

## Capability seams

A seam is Definition + Provider + Consumer. One role alone is not a seam.
Filesystem and subprocess share an execution world. Point both at E2B and Bash, PTY, and LSP move with them — no provider-specific forks.
ctx.sandbox.confine wraps local argv. It is a baby gate, not a move. Remote sandboxes are another fs+subprocess pair.

## Images and attachments (ctx.attachments)

Images are durable input-only attachments, never inline bytes in the log.
saveImage runs the admission policy, normalizes the raster to a deterministic canonical encoding, commits it content-addressed under DSH_HOME, and returns a serializable ImageAttachmentRef before any model-visible session event is published.
A SessionEvent carries the reference only — never base64, browser object URLs, provider URLs, or browser paths.
saveImages owns batch count and aggregate-byte limits and commits in order; a failed batch returns no partial references.
tool-fs registers read_image only while a durable ctx.attachments service is mounted, and refuses at execution unless the exact routed model declares image input.
dsh-llm-deepseek resolves each reference into a Files API file id, indexed by endpoint/API-key scope and request variantId (attachment id + transform version + pixel/byte budgets + encoder settings), with a seven-day default lifetime. Any resolution failure switches that request to inline data URLs.
Version one accepts PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF. Retention and garbage collection are deferred.

## Events — pick the domain first

- Session events: durable facts (turn/*, step/*, user/message, assistant/*, tool/*). Survive reload.
- Agent events (agent/*): live handle — inbox, status, pre-step, request, turn-stopping.
- Capability events: attach policy to a seam (fs/*, tools/*, llm/stream) without importing the loop. fs/observed is a plain emit fired after a read or write already succeeded; a listener must be synchronous and side-effect-only.

## Host and Client

Host runs in Node: webserver (dumb HTTP carrier), apiproxy (gateway). Native capabilities are loopback-only.
Client starts another Cordis Loader in the browser from __DSH_BOOT__. Slots compose UI. The window consumes session/event; it does not invent history.

## FAQ

Q: Which DeepSeek Harness version does this Brickbook cover?
A: The content is aligned with the official dsh-v0.1.1-rc.2 release at commit b150a55, published on 2026-08-21. That source snapshot contains 227 packages/*/package.json manifests; the directory curates the core and representative plugins instead of flattening all 227 into one list.

Q: What is DeepSeek Harness?
A: DeepSeek Harness (dsh) is an open-source agent runtime. It does not hard-code a model into its core: model adapters, tools, sessions, sandboxes, loops, and UI are all plugins. Its two central ideas are Everything is a plugin and Every run is traceable.

Q: What does Cordis do in dsh?
A: Cordis is the baseplate. Plugins contribute Services, typed events, and reversible effects to a shared Context. Registrations are automatically undone when a fiber is disposed. There is no privileged kernel to patch; extend the system by mounting a plugin beside the others.

Q: What does Everything is a plugin mean?
A: Every capability is a replaceable brick. Change the LLM adapter without changing the loop; replace the filesystem provider and Bash, PTY, and LSP can follow. Select, replace, and extend through configuration instead of editing dsh source.

Q: What does model-visible means logged mean?
A: Everything that reaches a model request must be reconstructible from the append-only Session log. deriveMessages() projects surface events instead of maintaining a second chat array. This runtime invariant is the basis of Every run is traceable.

Q: How are sandbox and E2B different?
A: sandbox.confine wraps local argv—a safety gate inside this room. E2B is another fs + subprocess provider pair, like moving the whole playroom into the cloud. A fence is not a move; hands and feet must share one execution world.

Q: Are Cordis inject and Agent.inject() the same?
A: No. Cordis inject declares plugin dependencies and waits for required services before activation. Agent.inject() puts a message into inbox.next-step without waking the driver. They share a name but do entirely different jobs.

Q: How are scope and isolate different?
A: scope is a set of per-agent lockers, not a sandbox. isolate gives a child Context its own service with the same name—its own classroom tap. Agent presets use isolate to change outfits.

Q: How do a turn and a step differ?
A: A step is one model request plus the tools it calls. A turn contains zero or more steps: it opens before the first input is claimed and closes when no work remains. Even a rejected first claim leaves a durable zero-step turn.

Q: Can dsh read images, and do images land in the session log?
A: Yes, but the log stores only a reference. ctx.attachments.saveImage validates and normalizes the image, commits it content-addressed, and returns an ImageAttachmentRef; base64, browser paths, and provider URLs never reach a SessionEvent. tool-fs registers read_image only while a durable attachment store is mounted, and the routed model must declare image input; dsh-llm-deepseek then resolves each reference into a Files API id and falls back to inline data URLs for the whole request when resolution fails.
## Module drawers

Each package group has its own page at https://dsh.177.best/en/modules/<slug> (drop /en for Chinese),
listing that group's packages with npm name, ctx key, and one-line job. Slugs are enumerated in
https://dsh.177.best/llms.txt.

## Where new behavior hangs

- New model provider → ctx.llm
- New model-facing tool → ctx.tools (schema joins prompt assembly)
- Different capability set per session → agent preset + isolate
- Shell → ctx.shell via ctx.subprocess
- Persistent PTY → ctx.terminals + dsh-tool-terminal
- Human slash command → ctx.commands (no model turn)
- Background work → ctx.jobs
- Filesystem policy → ctx.fs or fs/* events
- Durable image input → ctx.attachments (saveImage / readImage) + an image-capable route
- Confine processes → ctx.sandbox.confine(argv)
- Intercept request/tool/turn → agent/* or tools/* ; turn-stopping can stop a turn
- Model-visible context → Agent.inject()
- UI / editor → ctx.agents + session/event
- Durable session state → extend SessionEventMap

## Glossary

Plugin (Replaceable brick): A function or class that implements a Service. Function plugins export inject + apply(ctx); class plugins call super(ctx, name) in the constructor and register immediately.
Cordis (Baseplate): A spatially and temporally composable plugin framework. It contributes Services, typed events, and reversible Effects. Fiber disposal unwinds registrations.
Context / ctx (Shared shelf): The service repository. Stable keys include ctx.tools, ctx.llm, and ctx.sessions. Depend on a service name, not its implementation.
inject (Cordis) (Wait for friends): A plugin's service dependency declaration. Requirements express load order instead of manual boot sequencing. This is unrelated to agent.inject().
inject() (Agent) (Slide a note under the door): Agent.inject() puts a message into inbox.next-step without calling wakeDriver. Runtime context, skill bodies, and time commonly use this path.
Fiber (A mounted brick's lifetime): The lifecycle of a Cordis plugin instance. Fiber disposal unwinds every ctx.effect() / ctx.on() registration.
Effect (Reversible registration): Registrations made through ctx.effect() or ctx.on(). There is no privileged kernel to patch.
isolate (A classroom's own tap): isolate(name, label) gives a child Context its own same-named service. Agent presets use it to build a capability tree per classroom.
scope (Locker): dsh-scope partitions registration layers by agent. Scope is not a sandbox; isolate provides independent same-named services.
Profile (Toy box): A named assembly stored in Harness home. It lists bundles, out-of-tree plugins, and the user's cordis.patch.yml. Web and headless ship as templates.
Bundle (A ready-made bag of bricks): A distribution format for Cordis config entries and mounting code. dsh.bundle points at a patch file. Higher layers may always patch inserted content.
Patch (Note / sticker): applyEntryPatches replaces a complete config row by id or inserts a new one. There is no deep merge; later layers win.
Seam (Replaceable connector): Service Definition + Provider + Consumer. Extension plugins depend on the definition, never a concrete provider.
Execution world (The room where work happens): fs and subprocess share an execution world. Point both at E2B and Bash, PTY, and LSP follow without provider-specific forks.
Sandbox (Fence / safety gate): ctx.sandbox.confine wraps local argv. A remote sandbox is a different fs/subprocess provider pair, not a sandbox backend.
Session (Journal): An append-only SessionEvent log with in-memory storage, exposed as ctx.sessions. Fork, resume, and search derive from it.
Model-visible means logged (Seen by the model means already recorded): deriveMessages() projects model history from surface events. A runtime invariant ensures everything reaching a model request can be rebuilt from the log.
Turn / Step (One assignment / one step): A Turn opens before the first claim and closes when no work remains. A Step is one model request plus its tools. A rejected first claim still closes a durable zero-step turn.
Inbox (Notes on the desk): followup → next-turn and wakes; steer → next-step and wakes; inject → next-step without waking. Claim only deletes.
Waterfall (Passing paper through an onion): Around-middleware where listeners receive (...args, next). agent/pre-step, agent/request, llm/stream, and tools/* are waterfalls.
emit / parallel / serial (Broadcast / work together / take turns): emit does not await; parallel awaits all; serial awaits in order and returns values. turn-stopping is serial.
Host / Client (House / window): Host: webserver / apiproxy. Client: another Loader mounts immediately entries and gives the DOM to ctx.uiRenderer. Native capabilities are loopback-only.
Slot (A hole in the felt board): The SlotMap composition API. ConversationNodeDefinition plus a keyed renderer adds a conversation node.
Agent preset (Agent outfit): Assemble an agent + persona per session. Service rows require an isolate realm. Exposed as ctx.agentPresets.
compaction / spill (Recap / another sheet): compaction uses token-meter pressure to trigger summaries; spill moves oversized tool results out of line. replace removes nodes hidden by its shadow.
ImageAttachmentRef (Drawer number for a photo): The serializable reference returned by ctx.attachments.saveImage after it normalizes and content-addresses an image. SessionEvents carry the reference only; base64, browser paths, and provider URLs never reach the log. read_image requires a mounted durable store and a routed model that declares image input.
